items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its moving-average stack, then overlay the option-flow premium lean, contract count and the single most-unusual print and the VIX band, to judge whether an index holding near its high on broad breadth is being confirmed by demand or quietly hedged at the margin.
items.note: Breadth is broad but the premium tape leans mildly defensive into this pre-market window. The SPY benchmark last printed 766.08, only 1.52% under its 52-week high, in a bull-stacked moving-average regime (50-day distance +2.04%, 200-day +8.73%, 126-day momentum +12.52%), and 64.33% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day — a 4.33-point cushion above the 60% broad-participation line — even as a still-below-threshold double top stands overhead. Premium flow, however, reads balanced and slightly put-tilted: the call fraction is 0.45 across 12 tickers with 594 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days, and the single most-unusual print is a same-session SPY 766 put at $16.8M on 30.7x its open interest, sitting right at spot. So broad breadth and index price agree on a constructive tape, but option premium is not confirming with a bullish lean — it is closer to neutral-to-hedged. VIX 16.01 keeps this in a calm band. What to watch is whether breadth stays above 60% and premium rotates back toward calls to confirm the advance, or the overhead double top caps price while that at-the-money put hedge builds.
items.title: SPY holds about 1.5% under its 52-week high while daily breadth runs 64.3% above the 60% line, yet option premium is balanced-to-defensive and the most unusual print is a same-session at-the-money SPY put hedge

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative dealer gamma; flip=769.02; callWall=770; putWall=765; expectedMove=4.46; spot=766.14
items.method: Read the options-structure gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current benchmark spot, size the expected-move band around spot, confirm the dealer scenario and conviction from the gamma playbook, then overlay the intraday session type and VWAP and the VIX band, to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearest wall or whether the corridor holds.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price sit in a short-gamma corridor tilted toward the downside edge this window. Signed dealer gamma is negative, and SPY near 766.14 is below the 769.02 flip, wedged between the 765 put wall and the 770 call wall and much closer to the put wall than the call wall. The front expected move is plus or minus 4.46, so the modelled band runs roughly 761.7 to 770.6 and both walls sit inside it. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so sustained pressure toward the nearer 765 wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The gamma playbook reads range-break-watch with patient conviction, and the session is a range day under mixed control with VWAP 766.68 just above spot. This is a coiled structure leaning down: while 765 holds and VIX 16.01 stays calm it can stay orderly, but a sustained loss of the 765 put wall in short gamma is what tips the balance toward downside acceleration, whereas a clean reclaim of the 769.02 flip and then the 770 call wall relieves the corridor to the upside.
items.title: SPY spot near 766.14 sits below the 769.02 negative-gamma flip and nearer the 765 put wall than the 770 call wall, with a plus-or-minus 4.46 expected move that bounds both walls

items.method: Cross-read the real-assets per-vehicle scores and the 63-day driver block (crypto and industrial/energy equity proxies versus gold, broad commodities and the gold/silver ratio) against the equity sector rotation and the benchmark regime, to judge whether the real-asset bid is risk-appetite-and-cyclical-led or monetary, and whether it agrees with where equity leadership is rotating.
items.note: The real-asset bid and the equity rotation disagree on risk appetite this window. Within real assets, crypto leads — ETH-USD at 69.8/100 and BTC-USD 64.8 in uptrends — while broad commodities DBC 59.2 and PDBC 59.1 and industrial copper CPER 56.9 hold firm, and the monetary metals lag: gold GLD reads 42.8 and mixed while silver SLV 21.8 is weak; IBIT 47.3 and oil USO 47.3 are mixed; 14 vehicles scored on a swing horizon. The 63-day driver block corroborates the risk-on, cyclical tilt: the bitcoin proxy runs +13.51 and the energy and industrial equity proxies +8.65 and +6.59 against a gold proxy of only -1.26 and a broad-commodity proxy of +0.26, and the gold-versus-silver ratio proxy is +11.21, meaning gold is outpacing silver. Yet the equity sector rotation reads the other way defensively — into XLU (Improving, accel +4.58), out of XLF (Weakening), with XLV (healthcare) Leading. So the real-asset complex leans risk-on through crypto and cyclicals while equity leadership leans defensive; the tension is whether the crypto-and-cyclical strength persists or converges down to the cautious equity read. VIX 16.01 is calm and the benchmark holds near its high, so this is a rotation-quality divergence rather than a stress signal.
items.title: Real-asset leadership is crypto (ETH-USD 69.8, BTC-USD 64.8) and cyclical commodities (DBC 59.2, CPER 56.9) over monetary gold (GLD 42.8) and silver (SLV 21.8) while equity sector rotation turns defensive into XLU with XLV leading
